Mixing trials for rCF and thermoplastic fibers The goal of the mixing trials was to minimize fiber attrition, obtain good dispersion, obtain an end mix that produces uniform charge, deagglomerates the fibers and is able to scale up to RAM5 production (the industrial unit for RAM). Five mixing trials were designed as summarized below and in Table 8. • Mix test-1: High fiber matrix ratio provides deagglomeration and material volume expansion was observed • Mix test-2: Only carbon fiber was used to resolve the mixing ratio and fiber volume expansion was observed • Mix test 3: Decrease the overall amount of fiber and matrix; observe the material expansion • Mix test 4: Decrease the total amount further by 50% and fiber agglomeration was observed • Mix test 5: Using mix test 4 formulation 300 ml of water were added and the material dried overnight • Mix test 6: Using the test 4 formulation Table 8.Summary of mixing trials for RAM Figure 85 provides images of the material as prepared for RAM. Exact quantities mixed through the RAM process Table 10. Details of the rCF and polypropylene used 63 Carding trials with rCF-PP The mixed rCF+PP is then used as the source for carding trials. Carding is a process used in industrial nonwovens to feed entangled fiber stock and use the two counterrotating carding wheels to align (comb) the fibers into unidirectional mats. Carding works very well with wool, cotton and cellulose based fibers. There is very limited work with carbon fiber in carding. This study investigated the carding possibilities and successfully developed rCF-PP carded mats. There is fiber length attrition during contact with the carding teeth; however, several engineering innovations are ongoing to minimize the friction (force) on the fiber to minimize attrition. Figure 86 illustrates the steps starting with the RAM mixed rCF-PP, fed through the carding rolls shown, conversion into the mat, and pulling the mat off the carder using a Teflon carrier film to prevent collapse of the mats. Again, the eventual goal is to add this in-line to the SMC line where entangled rCF can be converted into carded mats before they enter the conveying belt of the SMC line. Figure 86.
